item.title: Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments
item.description: Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy [Getty Images] Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better". Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction". Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had" . The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested the deal may need to be renegotiated. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better." Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala? Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September. He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months". item.title: Jorge Martin on keeping MotoGP title hopes alive: ‘I didn’t do anything, it was in Marquez’s hands’
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin admitted that he lacked speed in the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint, suggesting he owes his slim MotoGP title hopes entirely to Marc Marquez ’s crash. The factory Aprilia rider arrived at Portimao needing to outscore Marquez by 24 points over the weekend to take the championship fight to the Valencia finale. But after qualifying five places behind Marquez in seventh, Martin failed to make any headway in the sprint, gaining only one position in the opening 10 laps. That would have let Marquez seal the title with a third-place finish, but the Ducati star crashed out of the sprint on the penultimate tour as rain began to fall on the track. Speaking afterwards, Martin admitted that he was lagging behind the frontrunners at Portimao, particularly with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi converting pole position into a dominant win. Asked whether he had kept his championship hopes alive, Martin insisted the outcome was never in his hands given the points situation. “Well, I didn't ‘keep’ anything. Everything was in Marc's hands,” he said. “For sure, it was a really tricky race. I didn't have the speed all weekend. Finally, in the race, it seemed I found a little bit extra. I was quite close to the podium fight, but I missed a bit more speed. “But in the end, I did my best. I finished in fifth position. Let's hope for a bigger improvement tomorrow. “When the conditions are really tricky like this, the focus more goes on riding because you need to be at 100%. “So you don't have room to think about anything. I was just really focused. I tried to fight the first few laps with Pedro [Acosta], trying to go in the front, and he was a bit faster. “We were catching the riders in front a bit, so this is good. I saw the places where I'm a bit slower, the places where I'm a bit faster than him.” Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Marquez has shown remarkable consistency since he returned from injury at the Italian Grand Prix in May, avoiding the kind of mistakes that have plagued Bezzecchi and Martin’s campaigns. The reigning world champion himself noted that his crash out of the sprint was his first real mistake in the second half of the season, coming just a day after he warned about the risks of racing with the title within reach. Martin said he understood why Marquez made an error at such a crucial stage of the championship, particularly with the weather conditions changing at Portimao. “Surprised? No. In these tricky conditions, anything can happen. “When you are in front, I can understand his position. Everything gets more risky, everything gets more stiff, as he said yesterday. “The problem for him was he wasn't alone at that point. I was behind Marc and Alex [Marquez]. So I saw the crash and then I relaxed a bit in that corner. Otherwise, maybe I would [also] crash. “So, this is racing and a bit unlucky. I thought he was going to make it [win the championship], honestly. So it was incredible. “I have another chance tomorrow, but anyway

item.title: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win
item.description: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win Celtic’s midfield required some personnel changes this afternoon, with both Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur ruled out through injury. That presented an opportunity for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan, and they seized their chance to great effect, both of them getting on the scoresheet in the 4-1 victory over St Mirren and make a good contribution to the overall performance and result Indeed, Oxlade-Chamberlain, who opened the scoring just after the half-hour mark, was also given the Man of the Match award for his contribution. Both players spoke to CelticPlayer after the game, and the England internationalist said: “I thought in the first half we were pretty good,” he said. “We played some really nice stuff with the ball. “We defended pretty well throughout the half, and being clinical when you get the chances is massive. "Today we were able to do that. That obviously sets you up to be able to try and control the game a bit more. “In the second half, St Mirren played some really good stuff, to be fair to them, and had moments where they controlled it, but the lead that we gave ourselves in the first half made it a bit more comfortable from there.” And Luke McCowan was also delighted to play his part in the win over St Mirren, which saw him score Celtic’s third goal just before the break. He said: “It felt great. I worked hard to keep myself in the position almost, but I was just happy to be back out there playing. “As he (Alex) says, being clinical really helps. item.title: Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them
item.description: Jul 22, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; former Alabama Crimson Tide coach and ESPN analyst for College GameDay Nick Saban broadcast during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images With just a couple of weeks left in the regular season, the College Football Playoff picture is starting to come into focus. And one of the most decorated coaches in the sport’s history thinks that only a few teams have what it takes to win it all. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban said on Friday that there are “three teams that have the right stuff” to win the national championship: Georgia, Utah, and Notre Dame. And despite spending more than two decades coaching in the SEC, he made sure to clarify that it was “no disrespect to Alabama.” Playoff Picture Taking Shape Georgia sits at No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings at 9-1, with its only loss coming against Auburn in October. The Bulldogs have won three straight since then, including a 48-21 win over Missouri last weekend. Utah is right behind at No. 2 and is one of two undefeated teams in the top five at 10-0, along with No. 4 UCLA, though the Utes needed a 40-39 win at Arizona last weekend to keep their perfect season alive. Notre Dame checks in at No. 6 at 9-1, with its only loss coming at BYU. The Fighting Irish have since won three straight, including a 31-24 win over Miami. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr were both named finalists for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award on Friday, according to On3. On the same show, Saban insisted that the SEC is still the best conference from top to bottom, despite the Big Ten winning three straight national titles. Yet only one of his three contenders plays in the SEC. ‘The right stuff’ Saban shared his picks during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think there’s three teams that have the right stuff. And this is no disrespect to Alabama, because I think there’s probably seven to eight teams that can win the championship, Alabama being one of them. But if you’re a betting man and you say, ‘OK, who can run the ball, who can play good defense and who has a good quarterback?’ You would say Georgia has that, Utah has that, Notre Dame has that,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban added that the rest of the contenders have weaknesses that could hold them back. “Everybody else maybe has a flaw somewhere along the way. Now they might be able to overcome it, but I think those three teams have the right stuff,” Saban said. That leaves out Alabama, which the committee has ranked No. 3, as well as No. 4 UCLA, No. 5 Texas, and No. 7 Miami, among others. Clearly, Saban thinks the national title race is a lot narrower than the rankings suggest. item.title: Redick Fires Up Lakers After Listless First Half vs. Kings
item.description: May 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick yells to his team during a play against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the first half during game two of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images The Lakers did not look like a championship team for the first 24 minutes on Friday. They looked flat against the last-place Sacramento Kings, trailing by eight points at the break. Coach JJ Redick had seen enough and decided to get loud . He did not sugarcoat the message to his squad in the locker room. “I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime… They may have a differing opinion of that. Can’t repeat every word I used,” Redick said after the team secured a narrow 106-104 win . The coach admitted his words were harsh but necessary to wake the players up. A Wake-Up Call for the Big Men Redick’s anger was not aimed at everyone equally. He zeroed in on center Walker Kessler , who had just six points, one rebound, and four fouls before the break. The coach told Kessler to be tougher and bring some energy. Kessler did not argue with the approach, noting that Reddick tore into him about it, and rightfully so. The player admitted he was not playing physically or going to the rim. He needed that push to find his game. Kessler finished with 15 points and seven rebounds after the halftime talk. He credited the coach for knowing when to yell. The contrast between the two big men was stark. While Kessler struggled early, Kings star Domantas Sabonis dominated with 15 points and eight boards. The Lakers could not let that happen again. Redick made sure they understood the stakes. “The main message was we’ve got to be tougher, we’ve got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick explained. He noted that some players might have a different opinion of his halftime speech. He would not repeat every word he used, but the point was clear. Stars Back the Coach’s Approach Even the biggest stars on the roster agreed with the coach’s methods. Luka Doncic led the team with 25 points and eight assists. He said the yelling helped get everyone fired up. “I mean, he yells, but I’m used to it,” Doncic said. He noted that sometimes it is good to have a coach who demands more. The team managed to outscore Sacramento 52-42 over the final two quarters. That second-half surge kept them from losing to a team with a 1-14 record. The game came down to the final second. Sacramento guard Zach LaVine had a chance to win it with a three-pointer at the buzzer. The shot clanked off the front rim, and the Lakers survived. The win lifted L.A. to 14-3 on the season. It was their second win in NBA Cup games. The victory was sweet, but the performance was far from perfect . The team has now survived close calls against weaker opponents all week. Per ESPN , the Lakers needed a 47-point night from Quentin Grimes to beat the Hornets on Tuesday. Redick knows that scraping by is not enough for a top seed.

item.title: ‘There’s a bigger issue people just don’t get’: Metta World Peace claps back after Stephen A. Smith’s racial Laker comments
item.description: Jan 7, 2020; Los Angeles, California, USA; Metta World Peace (Ron Artest) attends a game between the Los Angeles Lakers and the New York Knicks at Staples Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Los Angeles Lakers sit at the top of the Western Conference at 14-3, just ahead of the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs, despite losing superstar veteran LeBron James. European sensation Luka Doncic has firmly secured the reins of the team and is aiming to be an NBA scoring champ at the pace he’s playing. But the new roster selection has received criticism from some of sports’ most acclaimed commentators despite their hot start. After James left in free agency this offseason, the Lakers’ new-look roster drew plenty of reaction, especially from ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith, who couldn’t picture three white guys winning an NBA title in today’s league. But between Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler, the trio has averaged 76.2 points, 20.8 rebounds, and 14.2 assists per game. Recently, on First Take , Smith doubled down on his thoughts while openly asking “the brothers” around the league to step up and stop the Lakers, creating a media spiral of its own . Wednesday, former Lakers champion Metta World Peace pushed back against Smith’s take, making it clear he has zero issue with a white-run team. “I love seeing white basketball players on same team,” World Peace wrote via X . “I feel no less insecure about a majority white @Lakers. That’s like saying you are afraid of a black mom and black dad born president. People are so unaware that they are ignitors of racism. That’s like saying, my new semi chip company will not succeed because I’m a black board member. Let the white ball players rock and let our future black financial system principals and my new social impact go to market concepts rock.” Friday, in a video posted by Bassey on X , World Peace continued to defend his positioning but deepened the outlook as he believes there are other underlying issues that have been “brewing for years” in the NBA. “There’s a bigger issue that people just don’t get in terms of us players that are dope in sports. We charge for training,” World Peace added. “So now one of the issues is that a lot of us that’s out of poverty cannot afford even our services that came from poverty, which is why we do a lot of free work. So there are a lot of, you know, ethnic, you know, kind of, cultured individuals of the same ethnicity as myself that’s not getting the same training, because they can’t afford it.” It is not unusual for Smith’s comments to cause such an uproar, but his reaction will be interesting to see given that he has had a heavy political schedule for the past few months. item.title: Nikhil Chaudhary shines as Australia beat England in thrilling first T20I to take 1-0 lead
item.description: Nikhil Chaudhary produced a memorable all-round performance as Australia edged past England in a thrilling final-over finish in the opening T20I at the MCG to take a 1-0 lead in the series. Chasing 188 for victory, Australia held their nerve despite losing wickets at regular intervals, with Chaudhary and Jack Edwards playing decisive roles in getting the hosts across the line. Australia suffered an early setback when Jake Fraser-McGurk departed for just one in the opening over. However, debutant Sam Harper provided an immediate spark, smashing 32 off just 15 deliveries to give the hosts a flying start in the powerplay. Captain Mitchell Marsh contributed 37 off 32 balls but struggled to maintain the scoring momentum as England attempted to claw their way back into the contest. With wickets falling at the other end, Chaudhary took charge of the chase. He first stitched together a valuable 42-run stand with Marsh before combining with Tim David, who scored 20 off 13 deliveries. The duo added 48 runs in just 29 balls to keep Australia firmly on course. Chaudhary continued to find the boundaries and hold the innings together, but his dismissal brought pressure on the hosts. With 11 runs required from the final over, Sam Curran was handed the responsibility of defending the target. However, Edwards wasted little time in turning the contest in Australia's favour. Curran began the over with a loose delivery down the leg side, which Edwards dispatched over deep backward square leg for a six. The crucial blow eased the pressure, and Edwards went on to guide Australia home in the final over. Chaudhary's contribution with the ball earlier in the match, followed by his crucial knock in the chase, earned him the Player of the Match award. Earlier, England had posted 187/9 after being put in to bat, with captain Harry Brook leading the charge through a blistering 65 off just 20 deliveries. item.title: Oregon men's cross country misses NCAA podium by single point
item.description: The Oregon men fell one-point short of ending their long NCAA Cross Country Championships trophy drought. Led by a pair of all-American performances from Nick Griggs and Simeon Birnbaum, the Ducks scored 196 points as a team to finish in fifth place Nov. 21 at on the LaVern Gibson Championship Course in Terre Haute, Ind. BYU was fourth with 195 points, leaving Oregon off the podium for an 11th straight year. Griggs made his Ducks’ and NCAA debut Saturday, finishing the 10,000-meter race in ninth place in 28:45.7. Birnbaum was 23rd in 29:05.1. Oregon’s next scorer was Myles Hogan, who was 65th in 29:36.5, followed by Aiden Smith, who was 70th in 29:41.0 and Benjamin Balazs, who was 79th in 29:48.4. Also on the course for the Ducks were Tayson Echohawk (93rd in 29:57.4) and Evan Jenkins (205th in 31:00.0). Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto took home the individual title with a 28:27.7 finish. New Mexico, with three runners finishing in the top 10 and four in the top 14, won the team title with 69 points. Colorado was second with 107 and Alabama third with 109. Oregon women finish ninth The Ducks had a pair of finishers in the top 25, but there was a big gap between them and their other scorers as Oregon scored 312 points to finish in ninth place. Diana Cherotich was Oregon’s top runner as the Big Ten champ finished the 6,000-meter race in 17th place in 19:06.8. Juliet Cherubet wasn’t far behind as she finished in 21st in 19:10.9. Both runners earned all-American status – a third such honor for Cherubet and second for Cherotich. Dalia Frias finished in 58th (19:37.3), Ella Thorsett was 108th (20:08.8) and Ava Parekh was 185th (20:46.5). Finishing outside of scoring was Kendall Martin, who was 246th in 21:34.9. Sofia Thogersen, who had been the Ducks’ No. 4 runner all season, started but didn’t finish the race. Hannah Grapes of NC State was the individual winner in 18:44.3. Alabama won the team title with 120 points, West Virginia was second at 145, BYU was third with 152, and Northern Arizona was fourth with 215. item.title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence falls to 12% as frustration reaches new low
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to an NFL football game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction . That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have little belief in the current direction of the franchise. The continued decline in confidence is hardly surprising. The Colts have spent the past several weeks spiraling, and whatever optimism may have briefly surfaced after some of the front office changes has quickly disappeared. Poor offensive play, frustrating coaching decisions and the overall lack of progress from week to week have left fans with very little reason to feel encouraged. Rather than showing signs of a team building toward something, Indianapolis has looked like a franchise stuck in the middle of a messy transition. The biggest recent development, of course, is that Daniel Jones is now gone, officially closing the book on a move that never gave the Colts the boost they were hoping for. Jones had a few respectable moments early on, but the offense became increasingly dysfunctional under his watch, and it eventually reached a point where a change simply had to be made. His departure does not solve all of Indianapolis’ problems, but it does signal that the organization recognized the situation was no longer tenable. Even so, the quarterback change alone is unlikely to restore confidence overnight. The issues with this team go far beyond one player. Shane Steichen continues to face questions about the offense, the roster still has major holes, and the Colts remain far away from looking like a legitimate contender. At the same time, fans are now left wondering whether this next phase will at least provide some clarity about the future, even if the short-term results remain ugly. For now, this week’s 12 percent confidence mark says it all. Colts fans are not just frustrated, they are increasingly unconvinced that this franchise has a real plan in place. If Indianapolis wants that number to rise in the coming weeks, it will need to show something far more convincing than it has lately. item.title: Aston Villa frustrated by Sunderland in dull goalless draw
item.description: Aston Villa and Sunderland drew a blank in their Premier League match at Villa Park. Unai Emery’s team had the better of a game of few chances but failed to make the breakthrough and are now without a win in five games in all competitions. Sunderland, bidding to move away from the relegation zone, ended a run of three successive away defeats with the 0-0 draw. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Emiliano Buendia returned for Villa at the expense of Victor Lindelof and John McGinn , who was on the bench. Sunderland also made two changes, with Jules Ahoka and Wilson Isidor replacing the injured Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey. The home side were on the front foot from the off and forced a couple of early corners, which came to nothing. They had to wait until the 19th minute for their first chance, with Johan Manzambi’s low effort saved by Robin Roefs. The Sunderland goalkeeper had a let-off in the 40th minute when he gifted possession to Buendia but recovered to claim the Villa midfielder’s weak shot. Ian Maatsen threatened to break the deadlock in the early stages of the second half, but he could only follow an impressive run with a shot straight at Roefs. Soon after the Black Cats, who created little of note before half-time, forced their first corner but failed to produce anything worthwhile from it. Villa’s Leon Goretzka was then booked for pulling back Chemsdine Talbi, but Enzo Le Fee’s free-kick evaded Nordi Mukiele and was collected by goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. As Villa fans chanted for the introduction of McGinn, Le Fee fired narrowly wide. The home faithful got what they wanted just before the hour mark when McGinn was introduced, alongside Ibrahim Mbaye. The Scotland international had a chance to open the scoring midway through the second half but fired over. Sunderland won a free-kick 25 yards out when Goretzka fouled Le Fee, but the midfielder’s effort was straight at Suzuki. Villa boss Emery made another double substitution in the 73rd minute, with Brian Madjo and Ross Barkley replacing Nicolas Jackson and Goretzka. The home side pressed for a winner and, after McGinn failed to find the target three minutes later, Barkley forced Roefs to tip over a powerful effort from distance. Roefs reacted sharply to prevent Mukiele heading into his own goal, then Alysson fired over. The visitors almost stole a win in the first of three added minutes, but Talbi’s curling right-foot effort went narrowly wide of Suzuki’s far post.

item.title: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo
item.description: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo Jose Mourinho’s influence on the Real Madrid dressing room and slowly, yet surely grown, and the player now appear more hungry and prepared to win than they have in recent years. The opening phase of the season, which lasted until the first international break, saw Los Blancos adapt to Mourinho’s ways and even struggle to rack up wins. They were often dominated and scraped through games, which was understandable. After the first international break, however, matters changed for the good and the men in white began to look increasingly convincing. They began controlling games better and performing consistently, with the Clasico win marking their highest point. Phase 3 begins Mourinho has got Real Madrid back on track. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) As reported by AS in a recent update, Mourinho sees the new phase of the season that lies ahead of of the team as their third phase, and he is hoping for an even better run. By the time Christmas arrives, the manager hopes that Los Blancos are playing better football and that they have the UEFA Champions League qualification in the bag. If possible, he even hopes for a change on the league leaderboard with his side going on top. Mourinho’s plans have been moving as expected so far, but the manager is aware that the project is just getting started and that there is a long way to go. He has even proclaimed that reaching perfection will require ‘three seasons.’ Big games ahead Real Madrid have unpleasant memories of playing against Arsenal heading into next month’s clash. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Between the game against Celta Vigo tonight and the end of the year, Real Madrid have some big games to get past, and the third phase will be more challenging than one anticipates. For starters, Los Blancos will take on PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League after the clash against Celta Vigo, and will then go on a challenging three away-game streak. First, they must travel to Anoeta where they must take on Real Sociedad, and they then travel to San Mames for a clash against Real Sociedad. Both games, needless to say, are difficult outings and bring back unfavourable memories. Then, Mourinho and Co. must take on Arsenal away from home – a game that will bring back ghosts of the past. item.title: Bournemouth climb up to fourth after securing ninth victory in a row
item.description: Bournemouth extended their winning run to nine in all competitions as Evanilson scored for the sixth Premier League game in a row in a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Justin Kluivert was also on target to help Marco Rose’s Cherries climb up to the dizzying heights of fourth place in the table. The defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win over Manchester City before the international break. Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva. Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels. Bournemouth took the lead through Evanilson in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the in-form Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-footed shot into the roof of the net. Evanilson (centre) celebrates the opening goal (Steven Paston/PA) (PA Wire) Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from the edge of the penalty area which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area. Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of team-mate Tyler Adams. Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier. Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to forage a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for captain Morgan Gibbs-White but the England international could not properly connect with his header. James McAtee ballooned an effort over the crossbar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. Substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper Dorde Petrovic. Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and the Cherries’ third when he stung the gloves of Selz from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.

item.description: Getting a one-on-one look with Zion Williamson, Bennett Stirtz went to work. He shuffled his feet toward the baseline. The 23-year-old boasted his self-creation talent as he drilled a mid-range jumper. Also knocking down his catch-and-shoot looks, this was a sneak peek of his best-case scenario. The Oklahoma City Thunder survived an upset with a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans . This was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B play. Stirtz finished with 18 points on 7-of-10 shooting, two assists and two rebounds. He shot 4-of-6 from 3. He also had one steal. Since the Post-D.C.C. era started, the Thunder desperately needed complementary scorers. Stirtz had fit the bill on paper. But this was one of the few times that he materialized over to the court. Considering how short his leash had been this year, OKC decided to let him get creative and gain confidence as a bucket-getter. The result? Stirtz's best game of the year. He had a couple of straight-line drives to the rim. But most of his buckets happened in the jumper-variety. The outside shot fell for him. He drained his first high-leverage outside shot of his career in the final four minutes of this contest to put some distance on the scoreboard. Like Mara, Stirtz has been a contributor from the jump — albeit on rockier waters and in a smaller role. But the Thunder are hoping he can eventually enter a flow state as a scorer. Right now, he's still adjusting to the NBA. To the point that OKC hinted at wanting him to play much more within rhythm instead of overthinking things. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
